_comment: What happens to a command before it runs: relayed, pty, or native.
Spec 052, research.md D3/D7. One list, two readers: the shell adapter
reads this file at the prompt (through hooks/redlog-relay.py), and RedLog
reads it through src/core/terminal-class.ts. Two copies of these names
would drift, and the drift would be silent until the day an operator's
reverse shell went through a relay mid-engagement.
native: leave it completely alone. nc/ncat must stay locally suspendable
for the Ctrl-Z / stty raw -echo / fg upgrade (FR-025); an editor or pager
pty: brings its own TTY, so a PTY capture is lossless and the loss of
local suspension is a cost worth paying for these.
repl: interactive when bare, an ordinary command when handed a script or
wrappers: names that stand in front of the real command, mapped to the
flags of theirs that take a separate value — so `sudo -u root nc` is
classified as nc and not as root. FR-027.
